title: Permissions-Policy Header Blocked Camera Access for Face ID Biometrics
description: The security headers configuration initially set Permissions-Policy to 'camera=()', which completely revoked camera access for all execution contexts, preventing legitimate client-side Face ID biometric enrollment and authentication.
root_cause: Overly broad device hardware restriction in nutririsk/security.py specifying camera=() instead of camera=(self).
intended_behavior: Device permissions should permit camera usage originating from the application's own origin ('self') to enable biometric scanning while restricting geolocation and microphone.

trace.description: Client script requests camera stream for Face ID verification.
Security header middleware sets Permissions-Policy header on HTTP response.
Browser denies camera access due to camera=() directive.

conditions.description: User clicks Sign In with Face ID on a modern browser enforcing Permissions-Policy.

execution.attacker_perspective: A user or attacker cannot execute Face ID authentication because the browser sandbox blocks the webcam.
instructions: Click Sign In with Face ID
Observe camera permission denied error in browser console.
execution.observed_result: Browser blocks navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with NotAllowedError / SecurityError.

remediation.strategy: Update Permissions-Policy to allow camera for 'self' origin while keeping geolocation and microphone restricted.

likelihood.reason: Affects 100% of users attempting to use Face ID on modern browsers.

confidence.reason: Confirmed via source inspection and W3C Permissions Policy specification.

title: One-Time Password Code Preview Leaked in JSON Response When DEMO_MODE Unset
description: The /send-otp endpoint was returning otp_preview unconditionally in the API JSON response, which would allow unauthorized account takeover in production if an attacker intercepted or received the JSON response.
root_cause: The send_otp endpoint returned otp_preview without checking if the environment was running in production mode.
intended_behavior: In production environments, otp_preview must be None and codes must only be dispatched out-of-band via authenticated channels.

trace.description: Client POSTs to /auth/send-otp with an email address.
JSON payload returned to client included raw otp_preview.

evidence.description: Raw otp_preview was returned in JSON payload without production guard.

conditions.description: Application deployed without explicit DEMO_MODE=0 setting.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker calls POST /auth/send-otp with victim email and reads the 6-digit code from the HTTP response body.
execution.observed_result: Attacker receives the 6-digit verification code in the response body.

remediation.strategy: Guard otp_preview disclosure by checking DEMO_MODE, TESTING, and FLASK_ENV flags so that in production otp_preview is strictly None.

code_changes.fixed_code:
is_demo = current_app.config.get('DEMO_MODE', False) or current_app.config.get('TESTING', False)
return jsonify({'status': 'success', 'message': f'Verification code sent to {email}.', 'otp_preview': otp_code if is_demo else None, 'expires_in': 600})

likelihood.reason: Requires deployment to production without setting DEMO_MODE=0.

impact.reason: Bypasses authentication and allows passwordless account takeover.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated via API route analysis and unit test assertion.
